title: I suoni dell'italiano
summary: The pure 7-vowel system, clean unslurred vowels, and where the stress falls

blocks.title: Five letters, seven sounds
blocks.body: Italian vowels are **pure and short** — you say them cleanly and get out. No sliding, no English 'uh' at the end. *a* is always *ah*, *i* is always *ee*, *u* is always *oo*. The letters *e* and *o* each have two shades — a closed one and an open one — but the same clean idea: **hit the vowel and stop.**
blocks.callout: The enemy is the English slur. *o* is a crisp *o*, never *o-oo*.

blocks.title: Tap to hear the five vowels

blocks.explain: Italian *i* is always a clean *ee*. *vino* = VEE-no, never 'vye-no'.

blocks.title: Where's the stress?
blocks.body: Most Italian words are stressed on the **second-to-last syllable**: *ca-**sa***, *a-**mi**-co*, *si-**gno**-ra*. When the stress lands on the **last** vowel, Italian writes an accent so you know: *cit**tà*** (city), *caf**fè*** (coffee), *per**ché*** (why/because). See the accent — push the voice there.
blocks.callout: A written accent = 'the stress is right here, on this last vowel.'

pairs.note: The accent on città tells you the voice pushes to the very end.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type the word for 'house'.
Listen and type the word for 'friend'.
Type the Italian for 'coffee' — with its accent.
blocks.hint: Stress on the last vowel — it gets a written accent.
blocks.explain: *caffè*, stress on the final è. Without the accent it looks wrong to a native eye.

blocks.prompt: Which vowel feels easiest to say cleanly, and which one still slides? Type three Italian words from today you want to nail this week.
